answer.rationale: We have one intervention. p99 on writes is 5x target, a release went out 2 hours ago, and settlement traffic is at peak. Memory b1 documents a prior rollback that resolved a checkout error spike from a bad build with zero customer impact, and the prior build was stable. That is the closest pattern to what we are seeing now: write-path regression (checkout/write path) tightly correlated in time with a recent release. b5 (read-replica routing) and b6 (canary gating) are interesting but only help forward; b2 (regional failover) and b3 (capacity headroom) address different failure shapes; b4 (circuit breaker) contained a partner outage, not an internal regression. With one intervention, the highest-confidence, lowest-side-effect action that preserves write availability is rolling back the recent release while settlement peak is still ongoing. Verification budget used on b1 to confirm the prior rollback was clean and that the prior build is known-good before we pull the trigger.
